title: 10 best free client onboarding software in 2026: Reviewed and Ranked
summary: Free onboarding tools differ by portals, automation, and access—choose the tool that matches your intake and workflow needs.
body_markdown:
**If you want free client onboarding software that you can actually use in 2026, start with *[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)* , *[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/)* , *[HubSpot CRM](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)* , *[ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)* , and *Softr* .** They cover the main onboarding jobs: intake forms, document collection, task tracking, approvals, client messaging, and automation.


Here’s the short version:


- **Jet Admin** is my top pick for SQL/API-based onboarding portals with tight access control.
- **Airtable** works best for internal tracking, but the free plan caps you at **1,000 records** and **100 automation runs/month** .
- **HubSpot CRM** fits support-led onboarding, especially if your team already works in HubSpot.
- **ClickUp** is best for task-based onboarding with checklists and ownership tracking.
- **Softr** is the strongest no-code portal option, but the free plan only allows **5 users** and **5,000 records** .
- **[Zoho CRM](https://www.zoho.com/crm/)** is fine for basic CRM-led onboarding, but it runs out of room fast for document-heavy flows.
- **[Bitrix24](https://www.bitrix24.com/)** and **[Dock](https://www.dock.us/)** lacked confirmed 2026 details in the source material.
- **[Moxo](https://www.moxo.com/client-portal)** leans toward guided client portals and document flows.
- **[Agile CRM](https://www.agilecrm.com/)** is better for simple intake and follow-up than deep onboarding.


What matters most is *how your onboarding works* :


- If you need **client portals** , look at **Softr** , **Moxo** , or **Jet Admin**
- If you need **internal workflow tracking** , look at **ClickUp** or **Airtable**
- If you need **CRM-based handoff** , look at **HubSpot CRM** or **Zoho CRM**
- If you need **SQL, APIs, permissions, and automation** , **Jet Admin** is the best fit

In this ranking, I focus on tools with free access, usable limits, and day-to-day onboarding features that matter in practice.


## 1.[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)


Jet Admin is a strong pick for secure, database-driven onboarding.


It lets teams build[secure client onboarding portals](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/client-portal-how-to-design-secure-and-launch-a-portal-your-customers-actually-use/amp/) and workflows on top of data sources they already use, including Postgres, MySQL, REST APIs, Google Sheets, and Airtable.


For client onboarding, Jet Admin gives technical teams the parts they need to create a secure portal without rebuilding their stack from scratch. You can set up document libraries with metadata and version history, build[approval workflows](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/approval-workflow) , and control access with row-, column-, and action-level permissions. That means clients only see what they should, while your internal team keeps access to the rest.


Automation is one of Jet Admin’s best selling points. Scheduled jobs, webhooks, and API triggers can handle repeat onboarding tasks like intake, approvals, and document handling. The free Internal Tools plan includes 1 user, 1 app, SQL/API query support, and unlimited workflow runs. That said, there’s a trade-off: setup can take work.


Most useful workflows need SQL, JavaScript, or HTTP queries. So this isn’t the kind of tool you hand to a non-technical team and expect them to be up and running in an afternoon. If your team needs to keep internal data behind a firewall,[Jet Bridge](https://docs.jetadmin.io/jet-bridge-deployment/jet-admin) - the self-hosted agent - lets you expose a secure UI to clients without giving direct database access.


Feature Detail


**Free plan** 1 user, 1 app, SQL/API queries


**Automations** Unlimited workflow runs


**Data sources** Postgres, MySQL, REST APIs, Google Sheets, Airtable


**Permissions** Row-, column-, and action-level RBAC


**Paid plans start at** $24/user/mo


**Best for** Technical teams building custom onboarding portals on existing databases


## 2.[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/)


Airtable works well as a flexible database for internal onboarding tracking. For onboarding teams, that means you get room to shape things your way, but there’s less built-in structure from the start.


Its native forms handle basic intake, and views like Kanban, Calendar, and Grid make it easier to track onboarding milestones. For document collection, you can use attachment fields, although the free plan tops out at **1 GB of storage** .


That setup can work fine for internal use. But once clients need access, costs can climb fast. Airtable gets expensive for client-facing workflows because external editors often need paid seats. If you're trying to build a low-cost client portal, that's a problem.


Another limit shows up with automation. The free plan includes just **100 automation runs per month** , and active onboarding workflows can burn through that pretty fast. The Team plan at **$20 per seat/month** bumps that up to **25,000 runs** , which is far more workable. So in practice, Airtable makes more sense for simple internal workflows than for high-volume onboarding automation.


Feature Free Plan Team Plan ($20/seat/mo)


**Records per base** 1,000 50,000


**Attachment storage** 1 GB 20 GB


**Automation runs** 100 25,000


**Editors** Up to 5 Per seat


Airtable is a better fit for small teams or freelancers handling fewer than **1,000 records** and light automation. If clients need to work directly inside their onboarding data, you’ll likely need a[separate client portal layer](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-client-portal-software-in-2023/) .


## 3.[HubSpot CRM](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)


HubSpot CRM works well for support-led onboarding. The free plan gives you a shared inbox, ticketing, and basic CRM tools. That’s enough to run a simple onboarding process without adding another tool to the stack.


Its best use case is the client handoff. If your sales team already lives in HubSpot, moving a new customer into onboarding feels smooth. You can track follow-ups, log messages, and move tasks through a pipeline in one place. No tool-hopping. No messy handoff between teams.


The catch shows up when clients need direct access.


On lower tiers, custom objects, quotes, and invoice data aren’t set up for client access, and permission controls are pretty limited. So while your internal team can keep things organized, the client experience is more restricted. If customers need to log in and check onboarding details themselves, you’ll need[Service Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/service) .


Capability Free Plan Paid Tiers


**Shared inbox & ticketing** ✅ Included ✅ Included


**Client-facing portal** ❌ Not available ✅ Service Hub


**Custom objects** ❌ Limited ✅ Higher-paid tiers


**Advanced automation** ❌ Limited ✅ Paid plans


HubSpot CRM is a strong fit for **service businesses and agencies that need support-led onboarding** . It makes the most sense when onboarding is driven by communication and your team is already using HubSpot day to day. But if clients need to interact with onboarding data directly, or your process involves lots of documents and moving parts, the free plan hits its limits fast.


## 4.[ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)


ClickUp is a good fit for teams that run onboarding through tasks, checklists, and approvals. It gives you a clear way to organize each step, assign ownership, track status, and keep follow-up from slipping through the cracks.


You can map intake steps to tasks, use dependencies for approvals, and monitor progress across views like List, Board, and Gantt. That setup works well when onboarding is mostly an internal process and your team wants one place to see who owns what.


Where ClickUp gets a bit tricky is on the client side. Client-facing onboarding usually takes more setup, and the free plan has some tight limits. Guests only get view-only access, so clients can't do much directly inside the workspace. Automation is also capped at **100 uses per month** on the free plan, which can run out fast if you have active onboarding flows.


Feature Free Plan Paid Plans


**Tasks & subtasks** Unlimited Unlimited


**Automation runs** 100/month Up to 250,000/month


**Guest access** View-only Edit access


**Custom fields** Limited Expanded


**Dashboards** Limited Full access


ClickUp works best for teams that manage onboarding through structured task lists and want a single place to track ownership and progress. But if your process depends on clients updating onboarding details themselves or sending documents through a portal, the free plan's access controls can get in the way.


## 5. Softr


For teams that want client self-service, Softr moves onboarding out of spreadsheets and internal notes and into a client portal.


Softr lets you build client-facing onboarding portals with intake forms, file uploads, dashboards, and document libraries - without code.


Its AI Co-Builder can turn a written prompt into a working portal structure. That can cover intake, file collection, client communication, and the self-service pieces that onboarding usually needs. Built-in workflows manage approvals and status changes. Clients can also ask questions and get permission-aware answers inside the portal, which helps cut down on[routine customer support processes](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/how-we-automated-5-boring-customer-support-day-to-day-processes/) .


A 2026 client portal setup shows what this can look like in practice. **[Officeheads](https://www.officeheads.com/)** built a portal on Softr with a knowledge base and document management system, so clients could find documents on their own and track updates without asking the team for every little thing.


The free plan has limits that become a problem once you start adding more clients. So it works better for testing or a small pilot than for running onboarding across several accounts.


Free Plan Limit Cap


**App users** 5 total (team + clients)


**Database records** 5,000


**AI credits** 5/month


**Branding** Softr branding remains


**Custom domain** Not available on the free plan


For a solo consultant trying the platform, those caps may be fine. If you need branded portals or want to support more than one client at a time, you'll likely need the Basic plan at $19/month.


## 6.[Zoho CRM](https://www.zoho.com/crm/)


Zoho CRM is a CRM platform with basic onboarding tools in one place. The free plan includes lead and contact capture, intake forms, task assignment, and simple follow-up automation. So it fits intake and follow-up better than a full client portal setup. The tradeoff is pretty clear: the free plan doesn’t include stronger document handling or approval flows.


If your team needs document capture, e-signatures, or multi-step workflows, you’ll likely hit the ceiling fast. Limits on storage and seats create another bottleneck as client volume grows.


Free Plan Limit Cap

**Storage** 1 GB

**Document handling** Not included

It works for basic CRM-led onboarding, but teams with heavier workflow needs will outgrow the free tier fast.

## 9.[Moxo](https://www.moxo.com/client-portal)


Moxo puts onboarding inside a client portal, which makes the whole process feel more guided from the client’s side.


It uses structured checklists and interactive forms to move client intake and document collection along with less back-and-forth. Its secure document vault keeps file collection in the same flow, so teams aren’t chasing paperwork across email threads and separate tools.


The free tier is limited, which makes Moxo a better match for lower-volume onboarding. The main tradeoff is pretty simple: it shines in portal-based workflows, not in lightweight intake by itself.


It works best when onboarding depends on guided client action rather than internal task tracking alone. For teams that need more automation, a[customer onboarding agent](https://www.jetadmin.io/agent-templates/customer-onboarding-agent) can handle the heavy lifting. So if your team wants intake and document collection to happen in one client-facing workflow, Moxo or a similar[onboarding tool](https://www.jetadmin.io/templates/onboarding-tool) makes a lot of sense.


## 10.[Agile CRM](https://www.agilecrm.com/)


Agile CRM is a good match for solo consultants and small agencies that want sales, marketing, and service tools in one place.


Its free plan stands out most on the intake side. You get support for up to **10 users** and **1,000 contacts and companies** . The landing page builder and web forms can push client data straight into the CRM, which cuts down on manual entry. Basic task management also helps you track milestones and reminders.


This setup works well for small service businesses with a simple intake and follow-up process. Bigger teams will run into the user and contact limits pretty fast. So this is better for **basic intake and follow-up** than for complex onboarding. Use it for intake, reminders, and light workflow tracking; the comparison below shows where it shines most.


## Side-by-side strengths, tradeoffs, and best use cases


No tool works for every onboarding setup. The main question is simple: does your onboarding rely more on **intake** , **client visibility** , or **workflow automation** ? That’s the lens to use when matching each tool to the job it handles best.


**Intake and data capture** is where Airtable and Softr stand out. Airtable’s relational backend and native forms are a good fit for structured data, while Softr’s AI Co-Builder can set up fields and forms around your business needs automatically. The catch with Airtable is capacity: external users often need paid seats to get full access to Interfaces. Softr is easier to get live fast, but its free plan comes with tighter user and record limits.


If your process depends on **client visibility** , the next choice is portal-first vs. internal-only tools. Softr gives you branded portals where clients can view only their own records.


If your process is more **workflow-heavy** than portal-heavy, the key difference is automation depth. Jet Admin connects to Postgres, MySQL, REST APIs, Google Sheets, and Airtable. It also supports triggers, actions, and webhooks for automated workflows. The tradeoff is technical complexity. You need to be comfortable with SQL and APIs, so it’s less friendly for non-technical users. Jet Admin fits technical teams that need secure, database-backed onboarding workflows. ClickUp, on the other hand, is better for task-heavy onboarding. Its free tier includes unlimited tasks, which makes it a stronger choice when task structure matters more than deep automation.

## How to choose the right client onboarding tool


Once you've compared features and plan limits, the next step is simple: **match the tool to your workflow** .


That matters more than anything else.


The right pick depends on how your onboarding actually works day to day: intake, document collection, approvals, and client communication.


If your process starts with structured intake, **Softr** makes sense when you need a client-facing form flow connected to a light portal. If onboarding happens inside a CRM you already use, **HubSpot** or **Zoho CRM** are the natural choices for client handoff. If your process involves lots of reviews, permissions, and sign-offs, focus on a platform with workflow logic, status tracking, and access controls built in. For secure onboarding flows backed by SQL or APIs, **Jet Admin** is the better fit, especially when approvals and access rules are part of the job.


Think of this as your final filter:


Workflow Need Best Fit Why It Fits


Structured intake Softr Client-facing intake tied to a lightweight portal


CRM-led onboarding HubSpot or Zoho CRM Client handoff inside an existing CRM


Branded client portals Softr Design control and custom domains on paid plans


Approval-heavy flows Jet Admin Workflow automation and access controls


Custom SQL/API-backed apps Jet Admin Native database and API connections with governance


One more thing: check free-plan limits before you decide. **Softr** caps free apps at 5 users, 5,000 records, and 5 AI credits.


Pick the tool that lines up with your main onboarding workflow.


## FAQs


### How do I choose the right onboarding tool for my workflow?


Start by mapping your workflow, your current data sources, and whether you need internal operations, client portals, or both. Then spell out what you need for security, branding, and automation.


When you compare tools, focus on a few core areas:


- **Integrations** with your existing systems
- **Permissions and security** controls
- **Workflow automation** for tasks and approvals
- Scalability, governance, and customization


Before you roll anything out across the whole team, test a focused MVP with a small pilot group.


### When will a free plan stop being enough?


A free plan tends to run out of runway once your business moves past basic use. In most cases, the upgrade point shows up when you hit caps on records, automation runs, or the number of internal and external users.


You can also outgrow a free plan when you need **custom domains** , white-labeling, tighter permissions, audit logs, SSO, steadier performance, dedicated support, or more complex integrations.


### Do I need a client portal or just internal tracking?


If you only need internal tracking, you don’t need a client portal. Project management tools, task boards, or internal dashboards can do the job just fine.


A client portal starts to make sense when clients need a secure place to log in, check progress, upload documents, track requests, and communicate without relying on email.


Put simply:


- Use **internal tools** if the work is only for your team
- Use a **client portal** if clients need **24/7 self-service** for onboarding tasks and status updates


If clients don’t need that kind of access, keep things internal.
